Wavelet Peak Detection

Source: R/peak-cwt-details.R
peak_detection_cwt.Rd

Use step_measure_peaks_detect(algorithm = "cwt") to detect peaks with Mexican-hat wavelets at several widths. Positive wavelet maxima are linked into ridges; ridge persistence and local wavelet-space signal-to-noise ratio filter the candidates.

Choosing widths

algorithm_params$scales contains strictly increasing widths in samples, rather than measurement-axis units. The default is c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12). Choose widths that cover the peaks of interest on the sampled grid. Widths must be between 1 and 10,000 samples, with at most 256 scales. Each width must also fit within half the length of the finite signal run. The default width sequence is trimmed for short runs, including when explicitly supplied as integers or doubles. Other unsupported width sequences are errors. A run with fewer supported scales than the requested ridge length returns no peaks. Work is limited to 10 million coefficient cells and 200 million convolution terms per run; oversized requests fail before allocation.

Algorithm parameters

Pass CWT-specific controls through algorithm_params:

  • min_ridge_length = 3L: minimum number of linked scales.

  • gap_thresh = 1L: maximum number of consecutive missing scales.

  • min_snr = 4.5: minimum ridge SNR in wavelet space. Lower values admit weaker peaks and more noise candidates. This differs from the recipe's optional MAD-based snr_threshold, which is a separate filter.

  • noise_window = 31L: local noise window in samples.

  • noise_quantile = 0.95: quantile of absolute fine-scale coefficients outside the immediate peak support used to estimate local noise.

min_height remains in original signal units; min_distance remains in measurement-axis units. Nearby ridges can generate multiple candidates within one broad or noisy feature. Set min_distance for the separation appropriate to the measurement. Values nested in algorithm_params are currently not extracted as recipe tuning parameters.

Axes, missing data, and output

The location axis must be finite, strictly monotonic, and uniformly spaced. Irregular grids are rejected. Descending axes are reversed internally; returned peaks are ordered by ascending location. Missing signal values split the signal into independent runs, so detection does not bridge gaps. Median centering and reflected boundaries reduce baseline and edge effects.

Locations, heights, and detected bases refer to the original sampled signal. The additional algorithm_score column is the ridge SNR (capped at 1e6), and ridge_length records the number of linked scales. A local numerical noise floor keeps noiseless-input scores finite. These scores describe the detector, rather than a probability or a false-discovery guarantee.

Method

This implementation is inspired by Du et al. (2006), using discrete zero-mean, unit-energy Mexican-hat kernels and scale-linked maxima. Its ridge linking and local noise implementation are specific to measure.

References

Du, P., Kibbe, W. A., and Lin, S. M. (2006). Improved peak detection in mass spectrum by incorporating continuous wavelet transform-based pattern matching. Bioinformatics, 22(17), 2059-2065. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btl355

See also

step_measure_peaks_detect(), get_peak_algorithm()

Examples

library(recipes)

axis <- seq(0, 20, length.out = 201)
signal <- exp(-0.5 * ((axis - 5) / 0.3)^2) +
  0.7 * exp(-0.5 * ((axis - 14) / 0.8)^2)
data <- tibble::tibble(sample_id = "example")
data$signal <- new_measure_list(list(new_measure_tbl(axis, signal)))

rec <- recipe(~ ., data = data) |>
  step_measure_peaks_detect(
    algorithm = "cwt",
    min_distance = 3,
    algorithm_params = list(scales = c(1, 2, 4, 8, 12))
  ) |>
  prep()
bake(rec, new_data = NULL)$.peaks[[1]]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>   peak_id location height left_base right_base  area algorithm_score
#>     <int>    <dbl>  <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl> <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1       1        5    1         0          7.5    NA            21.5
#> 2       2       14    0.7       7.5       20      NA           173. 
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: ridge_length <int>
